title: Optiprep Gradient Preparation for Virus Separation
author: Ilana Gilg
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f6dbra6
materials: Make 25%, 30%, 35%, 40% and 45% Optiprep solutions in the labeled falcon tubes. You will need 2.5 ml of each solution for every gradient you plan to make. Mix well. For example, if you are making 2 gradients, you will prepare 5 ml of each solution as follows: 25% = 3 ml media + 2 ml Optiprep 30% = 2.5 ml media + 2.5 ml OptiPrep 35% = 2.1 ml media + 2.9 ml OptiPrep 40% = 1.7 ml media + 3.3 ml OptiPrep 45% = 1.25 ml media + 3.75 ml OptiPrep

Once all tube has been poured (all percent solutions have been added), seal the top with parafilm and place the tubes in the fridge. Allow the tubes to sit overnight to form a continuous gradient. NOTE : Tubes may sit in the fridge for several weeks and will still be good as long as they are sealed.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace
steps.instruction: UV and sterilize a class II cabinet with reagent alcohol. Wear gloves and sleeve guards to prevent contamination.

steps.title: Prepare OptiPrep Solution
steps.instruction: Aseptically collect OptiPrep solution into a sterile 50 ml falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Label five 15ml falcon tubes as 25%, 30%, 35%, 40%, and 45%.
Label one 50 ml falcon tube as "Optiprep".
Remove OptiPrep from the fridge and wipe the sides, cap, and septum with alcohol.
Using a 20 gauge 1/2 inch needle and appropriately-sized syringe, pierce the septum and aseptically remove 15-16 ml of OptiPrep for every 2 gradients intended.
Transfer the OptiPrep into the sterile 50 ml falcon tube.

steps.title: Assemble Loading System
steps.instruction: Create a gravity-fed loading system for the centrifuge tubes.

substeps.instruction: Attach the thin end of a pasteur pipet to a 5 ml syringe using parafilm or a rubber tube.
Secure the syringe with a ring clamp so the Pasteur pipet tip hovers just above the bottom of the centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Load Optiprep Gradient
steps.instruction: Layer the Optiprep solutions into the centrifuge tube via gravity, ensuring no air bubbles are introduced.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 2.4 ml of 25% solution into the syringe and allow it to flow into the tube.
Before the syringe runs dry, add 2.4 ml of the 30% solution.
Repeat this process for all remaining solutions.
If air bubbles occur, seal the top with a thumb and move the thumb up and down to increase pressure and restart flow.

steps.title: Load Viral Concentrate and Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Load the viral sample onto the gradient and centrifuge to separate viruses.

substeps.instruction: The next morning, pipette 0.5 - 4 ml of viral concentrate onto each gradient.
Balance tubes using sterile growth medium or the virus suspension solution if necessary.
Centrifuge in a Beckman Advanti J30-I using rotor JS-25.15 (swinging bucket) at max speed (40,000 rpm) for at least 4 hours at 8˚C.
Note: If separation is not achieved, spin for longer, such as overnight or 24 hours.

steps.title: Visualize Bands
steps.instruction: Carefully remove tubes from the rotor and visualize the separated bands.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes on a standing clamp.
If bands are not visible, suspend tubes in a beaker of water and use backlighting.

steps.title: Extract Viral Bands
steps.instruction: Aseptically extract the bands using a syringe and needle.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the tube wall with ethanol.
Use a 3 ml syringe with a 20 gauge 1/2 inch needle (do not use needles longer than 1/2" to avoid puncturing both walls).
If multiple bands exist, extract them in order from lowest to highest to prevent contamination from leakage.
Place the syringe just below the band, puncture the wall, and aspirate until the band disappears (typically 400 ul – 1 ml volume).
Immediately place scotch tape over the puncture hole to prevent leakage.
Transfer the sample into a 1.5 ml centrifuge tube and store at 4˚C.
